quote: I don't know if I want it or not. I just wanna find out what it cost.
stewart_read: This is the customer handing the rep a direct opening to ask 'what got you looking into solar in the first place?' The rep instead validates the price-only frame and moves straight to logistics.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged further probing as unproductive given the customer's flat affect and chose not to spend time there — a reasonable reactive-efficiency call, but not evidenced as deliberate strategy in the transcript.
coaching_implication: Coach Parker to use ambivalent openers like this as the entry point for the interest question, not a cue to skip it.

quote: The the bills average around that about 300 a month.
stewart_read: The customer gives a concrete, sizable bill figure unprompted-ish, but the rep only acknowledges it ('Okay. Gotcha.') and moves immediately into kWh usage questions without any emotional reflection.
coaching_implication: This is the exact moment for the ask+acknowledge+flip pattern — e.g., reflecting the $300/month as the reason the design matters. It was captured but never flipped.

quote: Do you know your login on on the Dominion website by chance?
stewart_read: Good process instinct — rep quickly identifies the customer doesn't have easy bill access and moves to find an alternative path rather than stalling.
coaching_implication: This procedural pivot (three-way call to the utility) is a transferable good habit; worth reinforcing as a model for other reps handling low-tech customers, per bill_collection.alternative_paths.elderly_low_tech_protocol.

quote: Yeah. If you just wanna hang out for a second, I'll add them to the phone so it'll be a three way call.
stewart_read: The rep commits seven minutes of call time to a utility IVR and live rep read-back. It resolves the bill-data gap completely and accurately (12 months of kWh), which is a strong data outcome for the design phase.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as time burn given the length, but the outcome (full 12-month usage history captured verbally, satisfying the required bill_amount / usage verify item) justifies the time spent — not flagged as inefficiency.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed here; this is the correct alternative_path execution when self-service access fails.

quote: is this a good day to show you that design and kinda go over the price with you?
stewart_read: The appointment gets a day and a time locked (noon tomorrow), but the rep never runs the button-up elements — no one-hour block statement, no no-driving/computer instruction, no 'is that fair?' handshake, no text-follow-up promise.
coaching_implication: Button-up is incomplete. Coach Parker to always close with the full sequence: hour block, sit-down/no-driving instruction, verbal handshake, and text confirmation promise — all are predictive of show rate and were skipped here.

quote: We'll plan to just have our specialist drop by tomorrow at noon, and he'll just kinda answer any questions you might have and show you the price and and the savings and see what we can do to help you out there.
stewart_read: The recap uses 'kinda' and vague framing ('see what we can do') rather than a confident, specific recap of what the appointment will cover.
coaching_implication: Isolated instance, not yet a cluster — but worth flagging if this pattern repeats across Parker's other calls; softeners here undercut the authority of the close.
